aiProse.executiveSummary: This report assesses the feasibility of refurbishing Hargreaves Teaching Block, a three-storey 1960s teaching building at Example University in Birmingham (1200 m² GIFA), to provide modern flexible teaching and seminar space with full systems replacement, upgraded fire safety, and improved thermal performance to support the university's net-zero plan. The estimated total project cost is £1,600,000 to £1,994,000 (excluding VAT), with a confidence grade of Grade A (High Confidence). The target completion date of 1 September 2028 is not achievable; the programme extends to approximately 28 May 2029, some 38 weeks beyond the target. The most material risk is the requirement to confine all works to vacation and holiday windows only, which significantly constrains the construction programme and creates a high risk of overrun into term time.
keyFindings: The project is cost-driven by full systems replacement across heating, ventilation, electrical, water and drainage, and data infrastructure, combined with asbestos removal and comprehensive strip-out and refurbishment of all finishes across 1200 m². The target date of 1 September 2028 is not achievable; the 124-week programme (including design, tender, and construction phases) completes around 28 May 2029, approximately 38 weeks beyond the target. The stated budget of £4,500,000 (including fees and VAT) is sufficient against the estimated gross range of £1,920,000 to £2,393,000, providing headroom of approximately £2,107,000 above the top of the range. The most significant survey gap is confirmation of electrical capacity and DNO requirements for the proposed air source heat pump system, which must be investigated during Stage 2 design. Traditional Single Stage Tender procurement is recommended because it suits public funding requirements, allows formal competitive procurement, and provides cost certainty through a fixed-price contract before works commence.
scopeAssumptions: The scope includes full replacement of heating and hot water systems via an air source heat pump serving the entire 1200 m² building, with external plant space included in the cost estimate.

The scope includes asbestos removal across the estimated 1200 m² of the building, strip-out of all existing systems and finishes, and installation of 18 standard and 3 accessible toilet facilities as specified by the client.

The scope assumes that the roof, recovered in 2011, and the south elevation windows, replaced in 2016, do not require further intervention; all other building elements are included in the refurbishment.
aiProse.costNarrative: The main cost drivers are the full replacement of life-expired mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems across the entire building, the removal of asbestos from an estimated 1200 m², and comprehensive refurbishment of all internal and external finishes, wall, floor, and ceiling surfaces. The specification of an air source heat pump system, combined with the need for enhanced fire safety measures, modern ventilation, and full data and IT infrastructure, reflects the university's net-zero objectives and the building's age and condition.
aiProse.roiNarrative: The project cost mid-point is £1,797,000, with an estimated annual operational benefit of £95,000, yielding a simple payback period of 18.9 years. The key financial risk is that the payback period is lengthy; if annual benefits are lower than forecast or if the project cost increases beyond the mid-point estimate, the return on investment will be further delayed.

constraints.title: Term-time working restriction
constraints.text: All works must be confined to vacation and holiday windows only, which severely constrains the construction programme and creates a high risk of overrun into term time if any phase slips.

constraints.title: Restricted working hours
constraints.text: The building is partially occupied during works and sits in the middle of campus; restricted working hours will extend the construction duration and may attract premium or out-of-hours rates.

constraints.title: Conservation area constraints
constraints.text: The site is in a conservation area or subject to an Article 4 direction; external alterations are likely to require full planning consent and the local authority may require enhanced materials and detailing.

constraints.title: Electrical capacity for heat pump
constraints.text: The proposed air source heat pump system requires confirmation of available electrical capacity and DNO approval; this must be investigated during Stage 2 design to avoid cost and programme impact.

constraints.title: Multi-phase delivery
constraints.text: The project is planned as multiple phases; the construction programme of 26 weeks shown is per phase, with an additional 34 weeks required for subsequent phases including re-mobilisation, extending the overall delivery timeline.

nextSteps: Confirm the asbestos management survey is current and scope-relevant; if so, it may be reused to reduce the survey programme and risk allowance. Obtain the asbestos register and verify it is a valid Refurbishment and Demolition survey.

Engage with the university estates and academic teams to agree detailed blackout dates for examination periods (January and May–June) and to confirm which vacation windows are available for each phase of construction.

Commission a Stage 2 electrical feasibility study to confirm the building's available electrical capacity and to obtain DNO approval for the air source heat pump system; allow sufficient time for DNO response in the design programme.

Seek pre-application advice from the local planning authority and conservation officer on the scope of external works (windows, doors, plant, and any façade alterations) to confirm whether full planning consent is required and what material and detailing standards will be expected.

Develop a detailed phasing strategy at Stage 2, confirming the split of works between phases, the re-mobilisation and interim closure periods, and the impact on the overall delivery date and cost; present options to the client for achieving the target date or securing a revised target that is achievable within the constraints.

riskRegister.description: Works are confined to vacation windows only; the 124-week programme spans multiple academic terms and risks overrun into term time when the building remains partially occupied.
riskRegister.mitigation: Phase works to align with vacation windows; agree blackout dates with faculty; build programme float; consider out-of-hours working where programme-critical.

riskRegister.description: Restricted working hours (Q3.5) extend construction duration and may attract premium or out-of-hours rates, increasing cost and schedule risk.
riskRegister.mitigation: Confirm permitted hours with the client; price out-of-hours working where programme-critical; reflect in Preliminaries.

riskRegister.description: The site is in a conservation area or subject to an Article 4 direction; permitted development rights are curtailed and external alterations are likely to require full planning consent.
riskRegister.mitigation: Seek pre-application advice on the conservation officer's expectations; assume full planning for external works when programming; allow for enhanced material specification in the cost plan at Stage 2.

riskRegister.description: Heating and hot water system uses an air source heat pump for full system replacement; electrical capacity and DNO check are required to confirm the site can support the demand.
riskRegister.mitigation: Investigate and confirm electrical capacity and DNO requirements during Stage 2 design; carry the outcome into the cost plan.

riskRegister.description: Asbestos is known or suspected in a 1960s building; the estimated removal quantity of 1200 m² is based on survey data and carries inherent uncertainty in extent and condition.
riskRegister.mitigation: Obtain a detailed asbestos management survey; establish a contingency protocol for unexpected findings; price removal at Stage 2 based on confirmed survey.

riskRegister.description: No services have been replaced since original construction; the building has ageing or inadequate M&E infrastructure that may harbour hidden defects or require scope expansion once opened up.
riskRegister.mitigation: Carry out intrusive M&E surveys at Stage 2; allow contingency for unforeseen remedial work; phase strip-out to reveal and assess hidden conditions progressively.

riskRegister.description: The target date of 1 September 2028 is not achievable; the 124-week programme completes around 28 May 2029, approximately 38 weeks beyond the target, creating a hard deadline risk.
riskRegister.mitigation: Confirm with the client whether the target date is firm or negotiable; explore programme acceleration options (long-lead procurement, phasing strategy) at Stage 2; establish a formal change control process.

riskRegister.description: Multiple phases are planned; re-mobilisation and phasing strategy are not yet confirmed, creating uncertainty in cost and programme for subsequent phases.
riskRegister.mitigation: Confirm phase split, re-mobilisation costs and programme at Stage 2; establish a framework contract or standing agreement with the main contractor to lock in rates and resource continuity.

riskRegister.description: Heating and hot water: Electrical capacity and DNO check — raised by the selected scope.
riskRegister.mitigation: Investigate and confirm during Stage 2 design, and carry the outcome into the cost plan.

aiProse.procurementNarrative: A Traditional Single Stage Tender route is appropriate for this refurbishment project, which has a clear scope, a defined budget of £4,500,000 and formal competitive procurement requirements under public funding rules. This route delivers the client's priorities of minimising disruption and achieving a fixed, certain final cost by locking the contractor's price at tender stage before construction begins.
procurementConsiderations: Confirm the phasing strategy and re-mobilisation costs at Stage 2; consider a framework or standing agreement with the main contractor to maintain resource continuity and cost certainty across multiple phases.

Long-lead procurement of major plant (switchgear, AHUs, heat pump) should be explored during design to reduce the critical path by 8–30 weeks; this requires early specification freeze and client commitment to advance payment.

Restricted working hours and vacation-window constraints will increase Preliminaries and may attract out-of-hours premiums; price these explicitly in the tender and confirm permitted hours with the client before design finalisation.
